reconcile.note: Clarke resolves the age arithmetic by denying Abram was Terah's firstborn, dating his birth to Terah's hundred-thirtieth year so the numbers align.

discrepancy.note: Troki showed that on Genesis' own numbers Terah died at 205, sixty years after Abraham left Haran — contradicting Stephen's claim Abraham left only after his father died.

quotes.text: This is erroneous, for Abraham quitted Haran during his father's lifetime. And since Terah, the father of Abraham, died in Haran at the age of 205 years, he must have resided there for sixty years after the departure of Abraham
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah), ch. XLV (1593; Eng. transl. 1851), on Genesis 11:32 and Acts 7:4.

sides.snippet: The days of Terah were two hundred five years. Terah died in Haran.
sides.verseText: The days of Terah were two hundred five years. Terah died in Haran.

sides.snippet: Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed out of Haran.
sides.verseText: So Abram went, as Yahweh had spoken to him. Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed out of Haran.
